summary: ShelterSim Studio's client is a React 19 single-page app where someone designs a passive winter shelter (box, cylinder or dome, sized in metres, with walls/roof/floor materials and windows) for a cold-region site like Ladakh and instantly sees a live 3D model plus a simulated 24-hour indoor temperature curve. Every edit in the left control panel writes straight into a shared zustand store; the centre 3D viewer (react-three-fiber/three.js) reads that store and re-renders immediately, while a debounced call to the studio-server's fast physics engine refreshes the results panel (charts, KPIs, plain-language insights) on the right. People can also register/log in, save designs, re-run and compare 2-4 saved designs' KPIs and curves side by side, and there's a marketing landing page with the same real viewer/engine wired in for a live demo. It talks to the sibling `studio-server` app only over HTTP (`/api/*`, proxied by Vite in dev) and imports types (never runtime code) from the `@shelter/engine` and `@shelter/studio-server` packages.

stack.name: React
stack.role: Renders every page/component and owns component state (forms, load/save status, loading flags).
stack.why: Its component + hooks model fits a form-and-3D-viewer UI whose panes need to re-render independently and cheaply.

stack.name: react-dom
stack.role: Mounts the React tree onto the page's #root element (main.tsx).
stack.why: Required companion to React for any browser-rendered app.

stack.name: react-router
stack.role: Client-side routing between Landing/Login/Register/Dashboard/Studio/Compare/dev-viewer, plus the RequireAuth guard.
stack.why: A single-page app with distinct auth/design/compare screens needs URL-based navigation without full page reloads.

stack.name: zustand
stack.role: Two small global stores: the ShelterDesign store (design/store.ts, what every control edits) and the UI-only 3D selection store (design/selection.ts).
stack.why: Lightweight, selector-based state that lets one field's edit re-render only the components reading that field, without Redux-style boilerplate.

stack.name: three
stack.role: The underlying WebGL/3D engine: builds wall/roof/floor geometry, materials, lights and the camera for the shelter model.
stack.why: The de-facto standard JS 3D library; needed to actually draw a 3D building in a browser.

stack.name: @react-three/fiber
stack.role: React renderer for three.js — lets the viewer be written as JSX (<mesh>, <PerspectiveCamera>, etc.) that reacts to design changes.
stack.why: Keeps the 3D scene declarative and in sync with React state (the ShelterDesign store) instead of hand-written imperative three.js code.

stack.name: @react-three/drei
stack.role: Helper components on top of fiber: OrbitControls (orbit/zoom/pan), PerspectiveCamera, Html (the PartPopover), Line, Edges, Billboard (compass label).
stack.why: Saves reimplementing common camera/controls/label primitives that every three.js app needs.

stack.name: recharts
stack.role: Draws the indoor/outdoor temperature line chart and the compare page's overlay chart.
stack.why: A ready-made, React-friendly charting library, lazy-loaded so it doesn't weigh down pages that don't show charts.

stack.name: tailwindcss
stack.role: Utility-class styling for every component; design tokens (colors, spacing, radii) are layered on top in styles/tokens.css.
stack.why: Fast to write consistent, hairline-instrument-style UI without hand-written CSS files per component.

stack.name: @tailwindcss/vite
stack.role: Vite plugin that runs Tailwind's build as part of the dev/build pipeline.
stack.why: Official integration path for Tailwind v4 with Vite, no separate PostCSS config needed.

stack.name: @fontsource-variable/geist
stack.role: Self-hosts the Geist variable sans-serif font used as the app's body font.
stack.why: Avoids a runtime Google Fonts request; ships the font as part of the app bundle.

stack.name: @fontsource-variable/geist-mono
stack.role: Self-hosts Geist Mono, used for numeric/unit fields throughout the UI.
stack.why: Keeps monospaced numbers self-hosted and consistent with the sans font family.

stack.name: vite
stack.role: Dev server (port 5273, proxies /api to studio-server) and production bundler/build tool.
stack.why: Fast HMR dev loop and a standard modern build for a React+TS app.

stack.name: @vitejs/plugin-react
stack.role: Vite plugin enabling JSX/Fast Refresh for React components.
stack.why: Required for Vite to compile .tsx files and support React's fast-refresh dev experience.

stack.name: typescript
stack.role: Static typing across the whole client; tsconfig.json extends the repo's shared base config.
stack.why: Catches type errors early and lets the client import server/engine *types* safely without pulling in runtime code.

stack.name: vitest
stack.role: Unit/component test runner (jsdom environment) for the 22 *.test.{ts,tsx} files.
stack.why: Fast, Vite-native test runner that shares the same config/transform pipeline as the app itself.

stack.name: @testing-library/react
stack.role: Renders React components in tests and queries them the way a user would (by role/label/text).
stack.why: Standard choice for component tests that assert on behavior/accessibility rather than internals.

stack.name: jsdom
stack.role: Simulates a browser DOM inside vitest so component tests can run in Node.
stack.why: Needed for vitest's 'environment: jsdom' setting since there's no real browser in CI.

stack.name: @shelter/studio-server
stack.role: Dev dependency only for its exported TypeScript types (ShelterDesign, Options, DesignSummary, etc.) that the client's api/* wrappers use.
stack.why: Keeps client and server payload shapes in lockstep without hand-copying interfaces.

stack.name: @types/node, @types/react, @types/react-dom, @types/three
stack.role: Type declarations for Node APIs, React, ReactDOM and three.js.
stack.why: Needed for TypeScript to type-check code that touches Node/React/three APIs.

folders.title: API client layer
folders.summary: Thin typed fetch wrappers (one file per server resource: auth, designs, simulate, locations, options, health) plus a shared client.ts that normalises every failure into one ApiError type. This is the only place that calls fetch() against /api/*.

folders.title: App shell
folders.summary: The outer page frame shown on every route: the header with the ShelterSim wordmark, Studio link and theme toggle, wrapping the routed page content.

folders.title: UI primitives
folders.summary: The small set of reusable form/layout controls (Button, Input, NumberInput, Select, Segmented, Slider, FieldRow) that every page and control section is built from, so the whole app shares one visual language.

folders.title: Design controls panel
folders.summary: The left-hand panel on the Studio page: one section per design concern (Environment, Geometry, Materials, Openings, Orientation, Advanced), each reading/writing the ShelterDesign store directly, plus shared helpers like SliderField and the debounced-request hook.

folders.title: Design state & selection
folders.summary: The zustand stores at the heart of the app: the ShelterDesign store (the single source of truth for the shelter being edited) and the UI-only 3D part-selection store, plus the pure PartId-to-control-field mapping and a small cached options-fetch hook.

folders.title: Small shared utilities
folders.summary: Two tiny standalone helpers: cx() for joining conditional class names, and the theme hook that reads/writes the light/dark/system preference to localStorage and the <html> tag.

folders.title: Results panel
folders.summary: Everything that turns a simulation response into something a non-expert can read: plain-language Insights (explain.ts), the KPI list, the temperature line chart, and the heat-flow bar breakdown, assembled by ResultsPanel.tsx.

folders.title: Top-level pages
folders.summary: One file per route: Landing (marketing home), Login/Register, Dashboard ('Your shelters'), Studio (the main design workspace), Compare, and RequireAuth (the auth guard), plus two subfolders for page-specific pieces.

folders.title: Compare page internals
folders.summary: The pure KPI-delta-table logic (kpiTable.ts) and the multi-design overlay temperature chart (OverlayChart.tsx) used by routes/Compare.tsx.

folders.title: Landing page internals
folders.summary: The marketing page's building blocks: the cinematic dark Hero with the live rotating 3D shelter, the shape strip, scroll-revealed how-it-works Stages, the live Chart section, and shared motion/visibility hooks (reduced-motion, in-view, animated hour).

folders.title: Global styles & design tokens
folders.summary: index.css (Tailwind entry, global resets, the native slider's restyle, scroll-reveal animation) and tokens.css (the light/dark colour, type-scale and spacing CSS variables every component reads).

folders.title: 3D viewer
folders.summary: The whole react-three-fiber shelter scene: pure geometry math (geometry.ts), the actual wall/roof/floor meshes with mitred corners (Building.tsx), camera framing, sun/solar position, the compass, part hover/click interaction, theme-aware colours, and the popover shown when a 3D part is selected.

folders.title: End-to-end test script
folders.summary: A standalone Playwright-core-driven script (flow.mjs) plus its own scratch studio-server, preview-server config and a hand-rolled PNG decoder (png.mjs) — not run by `vitest`; a manual, real-browser flow test covering register → design → save → run → compare → logout.

Declares the studio package's name, scripts (dev/build/test/preview) and every runtime + dev dependency.

The main end-to-end script: drives a real Chromium via playwright-core through register → new design → edit geometry/openings → 3D click-to-select → save → reload → run → second design → compare → logout → auth-redirect, asserting on screenshots, DOM state and network call counts.
A minimal hand-rolled PNG decoder (using only node:zlib) plus an edge-gradient bounding-box function, used by flow.mjs to measure the 3D viewer canvas's rendered extent before/after a design change.
A plain-object Vite preview config serving the built dist/ and proxying /api to the scratch studio-server, used only by flow.mjs's own E2E run.
Boots a throwaway studio-server (in-memory MongoDB + buildApp) on a given port, so flow.mjs has a real backend to talk to without touching a real database.
Typed wrappers for the auth endpoints (login, register, logout, getMe); getMe never throws, resolving to null on a 401 or network failure.
The shared fetch wrapper every api/* module calls: adds credentials/JSON headers, and normalises any HTTP error, network failure or unparsable body into one ApiError class.
Typed wrappers for the designs + simulations REST endpoints: list/create/get/update/delete a design, and run/list/get its saved simulations.
A single GET /api/health wrapper.
Wraps GET /api/locations/search for the custom-location search box.
Wraps GET /api/options, which returns presets, materials, glazings, ranges and defaults the whole app needs before it can render a design.
Wraps POST /api/simulate/preview, the non-persisted preview run used for the live debounced results panel.
Declares every route (Landing, Login, Register, dev viewer, and the auth-guarded Dashboard/Studio/Compare) inside the AppShell wrapper.
The real app entry point: loads the self-hosted fonts and global CSS, then mounts <App> inside a BrowserRouter into #root.
The page frame rendered around every route: wordmark, Studio nav link, ThemeToggle, then the routed page via <Outlet>.
A 3-way Segmented control (Auto/Light/Dark) wired to the useTheme hook.
The one button primitive, with primary/secondary/ghost variants — deliberately no other button variants exist.
Label + control + hint/error wrapper used by nearly every form field; also owns the 3D-part hover/highlight wiring (sets hoveredPart on mouse/focus, flashes when its part becomes selected).
Barrel file re-exporting every ui/* component and its prop types.
The base text/date/email/password input, with an optional monospace variant for numeric fields.
A typed numeric entry box paired with sliders/dials: keeps a local draft string, commits (clamped + step-rounded) on Enter/blur, reverts on Escape, arrow keys commit one step immediately.
A radio group styled as a row of segments, built from native <input type=radio> elements for free keyboard support.
A styled native <select> with a custom dropdown arrow.
A restyled native range input (the hairline-instrument look).
The collapsed-by-default 'Advanced' section: a single Occupancy preset selector.
Composes the six ordered control sections (Environment/Geometry/Materials/Openings/Orientation/Advanced) into the Studio page's left panel.
Location (preset site or custom search), date, and a weather-provenance note when the preview reports one.
Shelter type preset, Shape (box/cylinder/dome), Storeys, and Length/Width/Height sliders — hides Width for ring shapes and Storeys/Height quirks for a dome.
A debounced free-text place search box (via useDebouncedRequest + searchLocations) that lets someone pick a custom lat/lon location.
Wall/Roof/Floor construction (material + thickness) fields; opens and highlights the matching field when a wall/roof/floor part is clicked in 3D.
The four window-to-wall-ratio sliders (S/E/W/N), glazing choice and night-shutters toggle; each window slider is tagged with its PartId for 3D highlighting.
A drag-to-orient compass-dial SVG control for azimuthDeg, with pointer-drag and arrow-key support plus a paired NumberInput.
Wraps OrientationDial in a Section, wired to the azimuthDeg range from options.
The collapsible, titled group wrapper every control section uses; can be force-opened (e.g. by a 3D selection) without fighting a user's own toggle.
FieldRow + Slider + NumberInput combined — the one shape every numeric control in the panel uses.
Generic debounce-then-fetch hook: waits delayMs after the last input change, tracks an AbortController so a stale response can never overwrite a newer one, and exposes a retry() escape hatch.
Pure function mapping a 3D PartId to which controls section/field should open and highlight (window:o -> Openings; wall/roof/floor -> Materials).

A tiny zustand store for UI-only 3D hover/selection state (hoveredPart, selectedPart) — deliberately separate from the design store so selecting a part never marks the design dirty or reruns the preview.
The ShelterDesign zustand store: the single source of truth every control writes to and the 3D viewer only reads from — one setter per design field, plus loadDesign/reset.
A tiny cached hook around GET /api/options so every page/component sharing one request instead of each firing its own on mount.
Joins truthy class-name strings — the whole app's className-combining helper, no classnames dependency needed.
Reads/writes the light/dark/system theme preference to localStorage and applies it to <html data-theme>.
Turns raw simulation KPIs into up to three plain-language sentences (dawn temperature, hours below freezing, auxiliary-heat need, decrement factor), each tagged good/warn/danger.
Shared number formatting: Kelvin-to-Celsius conversion, one-decimal/zero-decimal formatting with negative-zero folding, and hour-of-day formatting.
A plain flexbox bar chart of the daily heat-flow pathway breakdown (kWh gained/lost per pathway), bars pointing left/right from a zero line instead of using colour for sign.
A plain hairline-row list of the nine exposed engine KPIs (dawn temp, min/max indoor, hours below 0/5°C, decrement factor, time lag, aux heat, kerosene).
The ordered list of heat-flow keys shown in the chart, and their human-readable labels, trimmed from the engine's full pathway list to avoid double counting.
Assembles the whole results pane for the latest preview: status line, Insights, TemperatureChart, HeatFlowChart, Kpis and weather-provenance note.
The 24h indoor-vs-outdoor line chart (recharts), with a custom tooltip and thermal-scale colours.
The client's own hand-typed view of the engine's documented (but not exported-typed) simulation result JSON shape, trimmed to the fields the UI actually reads.
The Compare page: pick 2-4 saved designs, fetch each one's latest run, then show an overlay chart and a plain KPI delta table (no scores/rankings) against the first pick.
'Your shelters' grid: lists saved designs with location/updated/dawn-temp, a New shelter action, and inline delete-with-confirm (no native browser dialog).
The marketing front door: fetches one real preview of the default shelter and shares it between the Hero's live temperature strip and the Chart section, composing Hero/ShapeStrip/Stages/Chart.
Login form: email/password, calls the login() API wrapper and navigates to /app on success, surfacing field-level or generic errors.
Registration form: name/email/password, same error-handling pattern as Login.
Auth guard for /app/*: calls getMe() and either renders the nested route (<Outlet>) or redirects to /login.
The main design workspace: three-pane layout (controls | live 3D viewer | results), loads/creates a design, debounces a preview request on every design change, and handles save-design/save-run.
Pure logic building the KPI delta table rows: converts Kelvin to °C, computes each design's delta vs the first (baseline) design, folds negative-zero, signs deltas explicitly.
Overlays 2-4 designs' indoor-air temperature curves on one recharts LineChart, one colour per design.
The landing page's live-chart section, reusing the same real preview response the hero strip samples — never a fake chart.
The full-viewport cinematic hero: an auto-rotating live 3D shelter with the sun sweeping dawn→dusk, forced dark theme tokens, and a live temperature readout sampled off a real preview.

Landing-only motion/visibility helpers built on native browser APIs: reduced-motion detection, min-width media query, IntersectionObserver-based in-view, an animated dawn→dusk hour sweep, and forcing dark tokens while the hero is in view.
Samples a real preview's 24h indoor/outdoor curve at a given clock hour, linearly interpolating between bracketing samples, so the hero's live numbers always come from a real simulation.
Three small live 3D viewers (box/cylinder/dome), each only mounted once scrolled into view so idle WebGL contexts never sit on the page at load.
The 'How it works' four-stage list, revealed on scroll via useInView + a CSS transition (respecting prefers-reduced-motion).
Tailwind entry point: imports tokens.css, maps design tokens into Tailwind's @theme, global resets/focus rings, the native slider restyle, and the scroll-reveal animation.

The CSS custom properties for the whole design system: light/dark neutrals, the accent colour, the reserved thermal colour scale, type scale and spacing — switches via prefers-color-scheme or an explicit data-theme attribute.

Builds the actual 3D building: mitred-corner extruded wall solids, windows, roof/floor slabs, for box, cylinder (12-facet ring) and dome (3-band hemisphere) shapes, wired for hover/select part interaction.
A ground-plane compass (ring + needle + block-glyph 'N') placed just outside the building footprint, always in true world-north regardless of the building's own rotation.
A dev-only route (/dev/viewer) previewing ShelterViewer against real options data with query-param overrides for geometry/hour, for visual QA outside the full Studio page.
Pure camera-distance math that keeps the scene framed regardless of the canvas's own aspect ratio (fits both a vertical and horizontal half-extent, takes whichever needs more distance).

Pure ShelterDesign → SceneGeometry conversion: wall/window placement and sizing for box/cylinder/dome shapes, mirroring the server's own facet-generation constants so the viewer draws exactly what the engine simulates.
A small floating panel next to a selected 3D part with 1-2 NumberInputs editing that part's key value, writing straight through the same ShelterDesign store setters the main controls use.

The top-level 3D viewer: sets up the Canvas, camera, lights, sun, ground, compass and Building, and wires optional autoRotate/interactive/frameShift behaviour for its different callers (Studio, Landing, Compare-less, DevViewer).

Independent implementation of standard solar-position astronomy (declination, equation of time, hour angle) converting a date/lat/lon/clock-hour into a sun direction vector matching the viewer's world frame.
A small disc placed at the real sun direction/distance, with a dashed line back to the building centre — only rendered when the sun is above the horizon.
Shared pointer-event wiring (hover/select) for any selectable 3D part, plus a colour-tinting helper for the hover/selected highlight.
Reads the current CSS design-token colours off <html> so the 3D scene's backdrop (background/ground/compass) matches the light/dark theme, re-reading on theme or system-preference changes.

flows.name: App boot
steps: index.html loads src/main.tsx as an ES module
main.tsx imports fonts + global CSS and renders <App> inside a <BrowserRouter> into #root
App.tsx (App()) declares all routes inside AppShell, lazy-loading the dev-only 3D viewer
The matched route component (e.g. Landing, Login, Studio) renders inside AppShell's <Outlet>

flows.name: Auth guard for /app/*
steps: RequireAuth.tsx mounts and calls api/auth.ts's getMe()
client.ts's fetch wrapper hits GET /api/auth/me; a 401 or network failure both resolve getMe() to null, never throwing
RequireAuth renders 'Checking session…' while pending, then either <Outlet> (authed) or <Navigate to='/login'> (anon)

flows.name: Edit a design -> live 3D preview -> debounced results
steps: A controls/* section (e.g. GeometrySection's SliderField) calls a setter on design/store.ts's useShelterDesign
The store's edit() helper patches the design object and marks dirty; only components selecting that field re-render
viewer/ShelterViewer.tsx reads the updated design, viewer/geometry.ts's buildSceneGeometry recomputes the scene, viewer/Building.tsx re-renders the 3D meshes immediately (no debounce)
routes/Studio.tsx's useDebouncedRequest (controls/useDebouncedRequest.ts) waits 400ms after the last design change, then calls api/simulate.ts's previewSimulation()
results/ResultsPanel.tsx renders the new Insights/TemperatureChart/HeatFlowChart/Kpis once the response resolves

flows.name: 3D select-to-edit a part
steps: Clicking a wall/window/roof/floor mesh in viewer/Building.tsx fires usePartInteraction.ts's onClick, calling design/selection.ts's selectPart()
viewer/PartPopover.tsx (rendered when interactive) shows a small NumberInput panel anchored at that part, writing through the same design/store.ts setters as the main controls
design/partMapping.ts's mapPartToField() tells controls/MaterialsSection.tsx or OpeningsSection.tsx which section/field to force-open and highlight via components/ui/FieldRow.tsx's flash effect
Selecting a part never marks the design store dirty or reruns the preview — selection.ts is a separate store from store.ts by design

flows.name: Save design / save run / compare
steps: routes/Studio.tsx's handleSaveDesign() calls api/designs.ts's createDesign()/updateDesign(), then loadDesign() on the response (clears dirty) and navigates to the real design id on first save
handleSaveRun() saves first if needed, then calls runSimulation(id) to persist a SimulationFull run
routes/Dashboard.tsx lists saved designs (listDesigns) and, per design, fetches its latest run (listSimulations) to show a dawn-temperature preview

routes/Compare.tsx lets someone pick 2-4 designs, fetches each one's latest saved run, then routes/compare/kpiTable.ts builds a delta table and routes/compare/OverlayChart.tsx overlays their indoor curves

flows.name: Theme toggle
steps: components/shell/ThemeToggle.tsx (in AppShell) renders a Segmented control bound to lib/theme.ts's useTheme()
Picking Light/Dark/Auto sets the data-theme attribute on <html> and persists the choice to localStorage
styles/tokens.css's [data-theme='dark'] block (or the prefers-color-scheme media query, for Auto) swaps the CSS variable values
viewer/useThemeColors.ts re-reads those CSS variables via a MutationObserver, so the 3D scene's backdrop colours follow the same toggle
